purpose: Define the shared uninstall/data-retention law beneath platform-specific package removers: normal uninstall preserves canonical Artist/Song/profile/recovery data, removable runtime state requires STOPPED plus exact non-symlink path evidence, package paths remain platform-managed, and held future services remain explicitly inactive.

lineage.outcome: Removing N0TE application/runtime mechanics never silently removes the Artist's durable work or activates held cloud/account/billing/telemetry/crash/DRM services.
lineage.capability: Shared uninstall retention policy and held-service absence boundary

legacy_rejections: delete runtime state while app is active
platform package path overlaps creative data
implement held services to prove their absence

completion_proof: data_root, exact profile_data_root and recovery root are always RETAIN_DURABLE_DATA and never removal candidates
runtime/config/cache/log paths are removal candidates only when app state is STOPPED, path evidence is canonical/non-symlink, and the path is disjoint from retained creative data
overlap with retained data biases to RETAIN_OVERLAP; nested runtime roots produce one parent candidate rather than ambiguous double removal
platform-managed package paths remain descriptive/non-executing and any overlap with retained/runtime paths is rejected
macOS, Windows and Linux path conventions produce the same retention law even when their physical root layouts differ
held services HOLD-001 through HOLD-006 remain HELD_NOT_ACTIVE with explicit promotion required
ApplicationRemovalPlanner exposes plan only and contains no delete/unlink/rmtree/package-driver/service-activation action
